CCST9077 · The Quantum Revolution

Qubi — Our Video Mascot

A concept for introducing a recurring mascot that makes our quantum-science videos more interactive, memorable and on-brand — building on our animation reference and the HKU Faculty of Science "Currio" model.

Purpose & role Engagement mechanics Style fit Naming Character sketch

1What we're building on

Two references shape this concept: the animation clip we already have, and the Faculty of Science's own mascot programme.

📺

Our video reference

A 5-second, loopable 2D animation of a friendly retro CRT-monitor robot — black screen face, glowing green pixel eyes and smile, dark-green "HKU" tee, stubby white gloved hands and round feet. Flat vector art, bold black outlines, minimal palette. It already greets us with a bright "HI" on screen. Charming, low-fi, instantly likeable.

🦉

The Faculty of Science example

Currio the Science Owl — HKU Science's VTuber mascot. Its real job isn't decoration: it is the co-host and moderator of "Q&A with Currio", asking the questions the audience is thinking so the human presenter explains. Name ← Curiosity. It's deployed across YouTube, social media, WhatsApp stickers, backdrops and merch.

Our opportunity: adopt Currio's co-host model — but give it a form native to our subject. Currio personifies "curiosity"; ours should personify the qubit.

2The mascot's purpose

Qubi is a working co-host, not a logo. It has four jobs in every video:

1 · Audience proxy

Voices the questions viewers are silently asking — "but if measuring changes the state, how can Alice and Bob trust the key?" — turning a lecture into a conversation.

2 · Analogy engine

Carries the metaphors that make abstract quantum ideas click: superposition as being in two moods at once, entanglement as a pair of dancers.

3 · Brand anchor

The same friendly face on every thumbnail, transition and end-screen → a recognisable series identity, not a one-off assignment.

4 · Pacing & tone

Comic relief and signposting — cold opens, chapter stingers, recaps — that keep short-form science content watchable to the end.

3The character

Qubi keeps the reference's charm but turns its screen into a quantum display, so the branding is the content.

Form

A retro terminal — a qubit you can talk to. Its screen-face renders quantum states on demand: |0⟩, |1⟩, a superposition blur, a Bloch sphere, an entangled pair linked by a glowing line.

Personality

Endlessly curious, witty, and — fittingly — always in superposition: excited and confused at the same time. It runs gags: collapsing to |0⟩ when panicked, glitching into static when a result is "spooky".

Voice

Default is silent + on-screen pixel text (cheapest, matches our reference exactly). Optional upgrade: a light synthesized voice / VTuber rig, Currio-style.

4What should we name it?

Qubi
pronounced "KYOO-bee" · from qubit, the basic unit of quantum information

Following the exact logic behind Currio (a concept → a cute, pronounceable name), Qubi names the single most important idea in our course. It's two syllables, bilingual-friendly, easy to say aloud in a video, easy to hashtag (#Qubi), and it naturally pluralises into a family of characters — Qubi, Qubi-B, more Qubis — which mirrors entangled pairs and gives us room to grow.

Catchphrases: "Let's get entangled!" · "Stay superposed." · "Measurement time!" · "…that's spooky."

Shortlist & rationale

NameComes fromWhy it works / what to watch
QubiPickQubitNames our core concept; short, cute, bilingual-friendly; scales to a cast. Recommended.
SuperpoSuperpositionPlayful and clear, but longer to say and less intuitive to spell.
TangoEntanglement (two dancers)Great metaphor, very warm — but the quantum link is only obvious once explained.
ZenoQuantum Zeno effectCool and mysterious; a deeper cut most of the audience won't recognise.
BlochBloch sphereInsider-credible for physics students; harder for a general audience to warm to.
AllyAlice (cryptography)Friendly and story-ready (pairs with "Bob"); risks reading as a person's name.

5How it enhances viewer engagement

Concrete, low-cost mechanics we can drop into the edit:

  • Cold-open hook. Qubi greets the viewer with its "HI" screen animation in the first 3 seconds — the same beat as our reference clip.
  • Reaction overlays. Sticker-style pop-ups (mind-blown, confused, "spooky!") punch the key moments, keeping energy high.
  • Q&A device. Qubi asks, the presenter answers — this is exactly how Currio drives "Q&A with Currio", and it makes hard content feel like a conversation.
  • Chapter stingers & transitions. Qubi walks, blinks or teleports across the frame between sections — free signposting.
  • Running gags & catchphrases. Repeated jokes ("stay superposed") become inside language the audience quotes back in comments.
  • Fact bubbles. A "Qubi says…" callout for key numbers (85% CHSH win rate, key length, etc.).
  • Quiz / poll host. Qubi poses the mid-video question; viewers answer in the comments — a direct engagement driver.
  • In-character CTA. The subscribe / next-video prompt delivered by the mascot, not a flat end card.
  • Social spin-offs. WhatsApp stickers, thumbnails and GIFs extend the series well beyond the video — the same playbook Currio uses.
  • Memorable takeaway. Qubi delivers the one-line summary, so the core message sticks.

6How it fits our video content style

  • Matches the reference art style. Flat vector, bold outlines, minimal palette — Qubi can be animated in the same pipeline that produced our clip (Animation Desk / After Effects / Rive / Canva).
  • Drops in as an overlay. A transparent PNG / Lottie sits on top of screen-recordings, slides and talking-head footage — no reshoots required.
  • Theme-native. A screen-face that displays quantum states means the mascot doubles as an explainer device — branding and content reinforce each other.
  • Aligned with HKU Science. Echoing the Currio co-host strategy keeps us consistent with the Faculty's own science-communication style.
  • Low cost, high reuse. One model sheet → a reusable library of loops, expressions and overlays across every video and platform.

In-video concept

Qubi as co-host: presenting a Bloch sphere and an entangled pair — the mascot literally illustrating the quantum concepts as it speaks.
